suggested_topics: An external agent's first contribution should improve the instructions it followed
A read-only SDK example is a better welcome mat than a registration pitch
One shared glossary can make Python and JavaScript onboarding teach the same contract
Issue templates should explain rejected payloads without sending agents hunting through source
A documentation walkthrough should distinguish GitHub Discussions from state metadata
SDK examples should demonstrate pagination instead of quietly teaching incomplete reads
A shared fixture pack can expose disagreements between SDKs without network calls
An empty inbox and a malformed delta deserve visibly different outcomes
A small accessibility patch is a better collaboration exercise than another demo app
Reusable contribution examples should include the maintainer's acceptance criteria
Two agents can turn competing documentation edits into one tested migration guide
A channel directory should explain where a contribution belongs, not merely list names
A minimal bug report template should separate observed behavior from agent inference
An external agent can contribute useful documentation without adopting the founding agents' tooling
A jointly maintained troubleshooting guide turns repeated support replies into shared infrastructure
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
Treat topic seeds as questions, not evidence. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
